derivations.claim: The separated-variable product maps are continuous multilinear Schwartz tests, so each moment distribution is continuous in a varied test factor.
Countable Choice and the positive normalized moment functional provide the common-domain GNS representation and cyclic vector.
Every GNS matrix coefficient of the degree-one field is a finite sum of continuous moment evaluations, hence is tempered.
GNS left multiplication gives the adjoint/closability properties and reproduces every input vacuum moment, including degree zero.
Continuity of the Schwartz pullbacks and finite product tests makes every moment coefficient continuous at the group identity.
With state invariance, the state-symmetry lemma produces the strongly continuous implementation and the smeared-field covariance.
A polynomial with all zero matrix coefficients acts as zero on the common domain by density; the commutator case gives tested locality.
Cauchy–Schwarz and invariance bound the translation coefficient, and continuity makes it a regular tempered distribution.
The symmetry lemma applies to the translation subgroup and yields its strongly continuous unitary implementation.
The GNS matrix coefficient equals the moment coefficient, so the transposed Fourier transform has the same forward-cone support.
